purpose: Predeclare the Phase C real-provider business outcome and runtime-ownership proof before the run.

positive_business_predicate.marker_generation: A cryptographically random non-secret marker generated immediately before the run.
positive_business_predicate.input_assertion: The marker is included in the submitted business instruction.
positive_business_predicate.output_assertion: The accepted business result contains the exact same marker byte-for-byte.
additional_assertions: The work run reaches projection_status internally_anchored.
The observed work_run.id exactly equals the recorded work_run_id.

external_paseo: Paseo runs in an external Compose service/container with a nonempty container ID.
The external Paseo container ID differs from the Agent Server container ID.
The external service owns the Paseo process, provider toolchain mount, runtime HOME/PASEO_HOME/XDG state, provider/model/timeouts, and provider credentials.
The external service depends on provider-toolchain-init.
agent_server: No Paseo process is present in the Agent Server container.
No provider toolchain mount is present on the Agent Server service or container.
No provider-toolchain-init dependency is present on the Agent Server service.
No provider/model/provider-credential variable is owned by the Agent Server service or container.
Agent Server connects to the external runtime only through PASEO_WS_URL.

cleanup_assertions: Cleanup is limited to the unique Phase C Compose project and run-owned temporary artifacts.
Cleanup does not prune Docker globally or delete operator-owned provider volumes.
After cleanup the unique project has no containers, networks, or project-scoped volumes.

negative_control.mutation: Run the same verifier with an explicitly nonexistent provider or definition.

rules: The expectation commit exists before the real run timestamp.
The real run timestamp is earlier than the proof commit timestamp.
The proof commit is earlier than the canonical-switch commit.
The expectation commit is an ancestor of the proof commit.
The proof commit is an ancestor of the canonical-switch commit.
